title: Patient Payment Plans Installments Counted in the Patient Financial Assistance Program Laboratory-Payments Deduction
content:
**Clause.** For a case under the Patient Financial Assistance Program, plan installments counted are added to the laboratory-payments deduction before it is rounded, by the standing of the household's payment plan in Patient Payment Plans:

- an active plan with no installment recorded missed within the last 6 months adds every installment paid within the deduction window;
- a plan that is past due or defaulted adds 50 percent of the installments paid within the deduction window, rounded to the cent;
- a household with any other plan or no plan adds no installments.

The amount is added to the laboratory-payments deduction itself, after the percent of the payments counted has been taken and before the deduction is rounded to the cent. "Within the last 6 months" takes missed-installment entries dated fewer than 6 whole calendar months before today.

| Plan standing | Installments added to the deduction |
|---|---|
| Active, no installment recorded missed within the last 6 months | Every installment paid within the deduction window |
| Active, an installment recorded missed within the last 6 months | None |
| Past due | 50 percent of the installments paid within the deduction window, to the cent |
| Defaulted | 50 percent of the installments paid within the deduction window, to the cent |
| Pending acceptance, paid off, cancelled, or no plan | None |

## Worked figure (hypothetical household)

The percent of the payments counted comes to $550.00. The household's plan is past due, and installments of $75.00 were paid on it three times within the deduction window, $225.00 in all. 50 percent of $225.00 is $112.50, so the deduction is $550.00 plus $112.50, which is $662.50, rounded to the cent. Had the plan been active with no missed installment in the last 6 months, the full $225.00 would be added, for a deduction of $775.00.
